PLAY WITH YOUR HEAD.

THE PLAYER’S HANDBOOK

The beautiful game,
one move at a time.

01 · Build the attack

The attacking team moves one piece, the defending team responds, then the attacker kicks. You may hold position during either movement step.

02 · Think like chess

Footballers move using their chess patterns. Pieces block movement; knights jump. The ball moves with its carrier. Pieces are never captured.

03 · Play the pass

Pick a highlighted destination. A pass stops at the first piece in its path, even an opponent. Empty destinations leave a loose ball to collect.

04 · Find the net

Send the ball beyond the pitch through either two-square goal mouth. Only kings may enter the four-square boxes. The conceding team kicks off with a fresh formation.

Tackling

A piece that can reach the opposing carrier using its chess capture pattern may tackle. Choose a highlighted red landing square beside the carrier. Both pieces remain; the tackler takes the ball.

Digital rule clarifications

The handbook leaves a few details open. Here, knight kicks are single L-shaped jumps. Other kicks travel any chosen distance along movement directions; pawns kick straight forward and tackle diagonally. Pawns do not promote. There is no check, castling, or en passant. Tackles and interceptions restart the sequence for the new attacker. A loose ball keeps the last attacking team until collected. Holding position and undo are convenience controls.

The match clock runs while play is active; pause stops it. Most goals at full time wins. Board box and centre markings are a digital interpretation of the handbook’s description.
